claims.text: Short-duration annealing at 300–500 °C induces partial ordering in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films.
The proposed annealing treatment refines the FeMnNiGeSi film microstructure.
A short 300–500 °C anneal can promote ordering while avoiding a full phase transformation.
As-deposited magnetron-co-sputtered FeMnNiGeSi films have a predominantly disordered microstructure.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films exhibit a sharp, hysteretic magnetostructural transition.
Formation of partially ordered crystalline domains reduces intrinsic strain heterogeneity.
Local partial ordering and a refined domain structure decrease the abruptness of the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Decreasing transition abruptness broadens the temperature interval over which the magnetocaloric effect occurs.
Moderating sudden lattice distortions diminishes hysteresis losses.
Annealing or partial ordering narrows the distribution of exchange energies, contributing to a more homogeneous magnetic response and lower hysteresis.
Annealed films will have a broader isothermal entropy-change peak than as-deposited films.
Broadening of the entropy-change response will be accompanied by a slightly reduced peak entropy change.
Annealing will reduce hysteresis by approximately 20–40% relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will improve magnetocaloric reversibility under low applied fields.
The predicted benefits hold for FeMnNiGeSi films of similar composition annealed for moderate durations at temperatures up to approximately 500 °C.
Excessive annealing time or temperature can cause grain coarsening.
Annealing-induced grain coarsening can negate the proposed hysteresis and magnetocaloric benefits.
Published data are insufficient to establish the optimal annealing regime or the magnitude of hysteresis reduction and transition broadening in FeMnNiGeSi films.
